messages:
marta: Quick update on the Corsair LoRA merge + quant smoke. Ran our 20-prompt quickpack across base(redwood/xl-7b), corsair-lora-v2, and quantized variants int8 and int4. Posting short results and next steps.
lee: awesome — hit me with the numbers + any obvious regressions.
noah: tl;dr: int8 is fine, int4 shows a small but noticeable amount-shift on invoice-like prompts. sample: expected "$1,200" -> model outputs "1,200 dollars" sometimes dropped decimals.
sophia: can you paste the eval summary?
marta: pasted below (quickpack aggregated):

```
model                       EM   F1   halluc_rate   token_ll_shift
redwood/xl-7b (base)        83%  89%  2.3%          0.0
corsair-lora-v2 (fp16)      85%  90%  2.1%         +0.02
corsair-lora-v2_int8        84%  89%  2.5%         -0.03
corsair-lora-v2_int4        80%  86%  5.8%         -0.18
```

notes: halluc_rate = flagged by our heuristics for numeric hallucination or invented lines. token_ll_shift relative to base (positive = more confident).
```

noah: ugh int4 looks rough on numeric fidelity. Did you run tokenizer checks too? corsair finetune uses a few vendor-specific tokens (SKU:, INV:).
lee: +1 on tokenizer. I remember Corsair added special prefix tokens for invoices. If int4 remaps embeddings slightly we can get aliasing.
sophia: did you try KV cache / streaming differences? sometimes the first-token sampling changes with quant kernels.
marta: ran quick tokenizer alignment: most special tokens preserved, but embedding L2 distance increased for 6 of 12 special tokens under int4 quant artifacts. quick diff: `mean_embed_delta = 0.004 (int8) vs 0.032 (int4)`
noah: that's telling. Could be quantization scale mismatch on the adapter patch. Is the LoRA merged before quant or after?
marta: merged then quantized with qlora-ish pipeline (merge->merge-clip->quant). We used the standard squeeze-clip step. Config snippet: 
```
commit: a1b2c3d
merge_cmd: tools/merge_lora --base redwood/xl-7b --lora corsair-lora-v2 --out merged/corsair-v2
quant_cmd: tools/quantize --model merged/corsair-v2 --bits 4 --method blockwise --calib 1024
```

lee: maybe try quantizing the base first then apply a patched adapter re-finetune (2-3 steps) — sometimes that preserves special token geometry.
sophia: or apply per-token bias correction post-quant. We did that for another customer and it fixed small numeric shifts.
marta: good ideas. Also to note: human spot-check shows int4 gives slightly longer, more verbose currency formatting ("one thousand two hundred dollars") while base/FP16 usually emits symbol+number. QA bot found 7/200 prompts with formatting diffs; threshold is 10/200 so still acceptable for a canary but not for full rollout.
qa-bot: quickpack run finished. regressions flagged: 7 formatting, 3 hallucination markers, 1 deterministic-decode timeout (streaming). See /evals/quickpacks/1745506789-report.json
noah: streaming timeout — which runtime kernel?
marta: it happened on our new 4-bit CUDA kernel (v2), fallback to CPU for that request in logs. stack: `runtime-gpu-v2 -> kernel-quant4-stream`.
lee: action items: 1) try post-quant per-token bias fix (sophia), 2) rerun merge->quant with alternate pipeline (lee + marta), 3) expand quickpack by +50 invoice-like prompts (noah), 4) block canary if halluc_rate hits >3.5% on expanded set (sophia).
sophia: I'll own per-token bias patch prototype, ETA end of day tomorrow.
noah: I'll add 50 more invoice prompts and run overnight. will post results here.
marta: I'll try base-quant-first pipeline tonight and post kernel logs.
lee: thanks. if anyone wants to reproduce locally:
```
# reproduce quickpack locally
git checkout a1b2c3d
python tools/run_quickpack.py --model merged/corsair-v2 --prompts ./evals/corsair-invoice-20.json --out quickruns/1745506789
```

sophia: thumbs up. tagging @deploy-bot — do not promote int4 variant to canary yet.
deploy-bot: noted. Promotion blocked for `corsair-lora-v2_int4` pending follow-up. :no_entry_sign:
marta: we'll reconvene after the overnight runs. thanks team! :rocket:
